newsitem.title: UK: Ghana adviser accepts libel damages over drug slur.
newsitem.headline: Ghana adviser accepts libel damages over drug slur.

text.p: A leading Ghanaian security officer and presidential adviser on Monday accepted substantial but undisclosed damages in London's High Court over a magazine article implicating him in the drug trade.
Lawyers for the magazine New African apologised in court and acknowledged that allegations in its April 1996 issue against Captain Kojo Tsikata were "utterly false and should never have been made".
Tsikata is a member of the Council of State of Ghana and national security adviser to President Jerry Rawlings.
The magazine article called "Ghana: Corruption at the Top" had implicated Tsikata in drug trading, the purchase of arms, and the fraudulent issue of diplomatic passports to drug dealers.
The magazine agreed to pay court costs and substantial damages to Tsikata, whose lawyers said the money would be donated to two Ghanaian charities.
